headline: Inflation in Mexico accelerated to 3.96% in the first half of November, its highest level since May
summary: Mexico's annual inflation rose to 3.96% in the first half of November 2026, its highest level since May. Higher electricity prices and vegetables such as tomatoes drove the increase.
why: Inflation data shapes the Banco de México's interest rate decisions, which influence peso bonds and the currency. Price pressures are closely watched by foreign investors in Mexican assets.
original_headline: Inflación en México se aceleró a 3.96% en la primera quincena de noviembre, su mayor nivel desde mayo
